exercises.title: Priority customers with missing or substantial credit
exercises.instructions: Display names and credit limits for customers in Antwerp, Ghent or Leuven who either have no recorded credit limit or have a limit of at least 2500. Sort the result by city and then surname.
exercises.provenance: sql-cheat-sheet.md; sql.md (course scope and exercise specification)
exercises.referenceSolution: SELECT first_name, last_name, city, credit_limit FROM customers WHERE city IN ('Antwerp', 'Ghent', 'Leuven') AND (credit_limit IS NULL OR credit_limit >= 2500) ORDER BY city, last_name;
hints: Combine a city membership test with a parenthesized OR condition for credit values.
exercises.explanation: The city filter is applied together with either a missing credit limit or a sufficiently high known limit; ORDER BY then sorts the matching customers.

exercises.title: Student registration with teacher and subject area
exercises.instructions: Display student names, course subject areas and teacher names for each enrollment.
exercises.provenance: sql-cheat-sheet.md; sql.md (course scope and exercise specification)
exercises.referenceSolution: SELECT st.first_name, st.last_name, c.subject_area, t.first_name AS teacher_first_name, t.last_name AS teacher_last_name FROM enrollments e JOIN students st ON e.student_id = st.student_id JOIN class_sections s ON e.section_id = s.section_id AND e.course_id = s.course_id JOIN courses c ON s.course_id = c.course_id JOIN teachers t ON s.teacher_id = t.teacher_id;
hints: Follow the enrollment through its student, matching section, course and assigned teacher.
exercises.explanation: The joins trace the enrollment relationships to retrieve the student, course subject and teacher details.

exercises.title: Find premium products in their price range
exercises.instructions: Display product names and band labels for products priced from 100 through 500 inclusive.
exercises.provenance: sql-cheat-sheet.md; sql.md (course scope and exercise specification)
exercises.referenceSolution: SELECT p.product_name, p.unit_price, b.band_label FROM products p JOIN price_bands b ON p.unit_price >= b.min_price AND p.unit_price <= b.max_price WHERE p.unit_price BETWEEN 100 AND 500 ORDER BY p.unit_price DESC;
hints: Use a range-based join, then apply an inclusive range filter and sort the matched products.
exercises.explanation: The non-equi join assigns a band based on its bounds; BETWEEN restricts the displayed products to the requested inclusive price range.

exercises.title: Find consultant pairs with increasing rates
exercises.instructions: List consultant pairs where both consultants share a specialty and the first consultant has a lower hourly rate than the second. Display both names and rates.
exercises.provenance: sql-cheat-sheet.md; sql.md (course scope and exercise specification)
exercises.referenceSolution: SELECT c1.first_name, c1.last_name, c1.hourly_rate, c2.first_name AS other_first_name, c2.last_name AS other_last_name, c2.hourly_rate AS other_rate FROM consultants c1 JOIN consultants c2 ON c1.specialty = c2.specialty AND c1.hourly_rate < c2.hourly_rate;
hints: Match the specialty and compare the two rate values in the same join condition.
exercises.explanation: The self join matches consultants in the same specialty and retains pair directions where the first rate is lower.

exercises.title: Highest sales total per shipping city threshold
exercises.instructions: Display shipping cities and the total order-line value for each city, considering only orders placed in 2025 and keeping cities whose total value is above 700.
exercises.provenance: sql-cheat-sheet.md; sql.md (course scope and exercise specification)
exercises.referenceSolution: SELECT o.shipping_city, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS city_sales FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.order_date BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY o.shipping_city HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 700;
hints: Filter the joined order rows by date, group by shipping city and filter the aggregate total.
exercises.explanation: The date condition restricts the rows before grouping; SUM calculates city sales, and HAVING keeps cities whose total exceeds 700.
